n: After rebuking Israel, God turns with surprising tenderness: the One who created you says don’t be afraid—I have redeemed you, I have called you by name, you are Mine. Each person belongs to God personally.

f.w: I have called thee by thy name

n: God doesn’t promise to keep us out of floods and fire, but to be with us in them. It recalls crossing the Red Sea and the Jordan, and the three young men in the fiery furnace.

f.w: When thou passest through the waters
when thou walkest through the fire

n: As Savior, God paid a ransom for Israel, giving up Egypt, Cush, and Seba—lands Persia later conquered after freeing the Jews. The point is how much Israel is worth to Him.

f.g: A people of the Nile region south of Egypt, or southern Arabia.

n: Because you are precious, honored, and loved by Me, I would give nations in exchange for you. Few verses express God’s love more directly.

f.w: thou wast precious in my sight

n: The promise of gathering: God will bring Israel’s descendants from east and west. Latter-day Saints see this fulfilled both in the return from Babylon and in the latter-day gathering of Israel.

f.w: I will bring thy seed from the east

n: God commands north and south to release His sons and daughters from the ends of the earth.

f.w: bring my sons from far, and my daughters

n: Everyone called by God’s name—His covenant people—was created for His glory. Taking His name brings identity and purpose.

f.w: every one that is called by my name

n: Bring out the people who have eyes and ears but haven’t used them—Israel, called again as witnesses despite their blindness.

f.w: the blind people that have eyes

n: Another courtroom scene: let the nations gather and produce witnesses that their gods predicted history. If they can’t, let them admit the truth.
Israel is God’s witness. No god was formed before Him or will be after Him—He alone is God for Israel. Latter-day Saints also understand Jehovah here to be the premortal Christ.

f.w: before me there was no God formed

n: There is no Savior but the Lord. Latter-day Saints read this as a witness that Jehovah is Jesus Christ, the only source of salvation.

f.w: beside me there is no saviour

n: God announced, saved, and revealed when no foreign god was among them. Israel’s own history testifies that He is God.
From before time began He is the same. No one can snatch anything from His hand, and no one can stop what He does.

f.w: none that can deliver out of my hand

n: For Israel’s sake God will send against Babylon and bring down the Chaldeans, whose ships were their pride. The empire that captured Judah will itself fall.

f.g: The ruling people of the Neo-Babylonian empire.

f.w: whose cry is in the ships
f.g: Babylon was proud of river and sea trade; the phrase may also picture them fleeing by boat.

n: God names Himself: your Holy One, Israel’s Creator, your King.
He reminds them He once opened a path through the sea—the Exodus.

f.w: maketh a way in the sea

n: Pharaoh’s chariots and army lay down and never got up, snuffed out like a wick.

f.g: Flax fibers used as a lamp wick.

n: Surprisingly, God says: don’t dwell on the past. What He is about to do will be even greater than the Exodus.

f.w: Remember ye not the former things

n: “I am doing a new thing; can’t you see it sprouting?” A new Exodus is coming—a road in the wilderness and rivers in the desert as God brings His people home.

f.w: I will do a new thing

n: Even wild animals will honor God for the water He provides His chosen people in the desert.
God formed this people for Himself so they would declare His praise.

f.w: they shall shew forth my praise

n: The tone turns: yet Israel hasn’t called on Him; they have grown weary of Him.
God says He didn’t burden them with demands, yet they failed to honor Him even in the worship He asked. Perhaps their offerings had become empty or were impossible in exile.
They didn’t buy Him fragrant cane or bring rich offerings. Instead they turned things around—they burdened Him with their sins. Here is a hint of the Savior bearing the weight of sin.

f.g: Calamus, a fragrant reed used in the holy anointing oil (Exodus 30:23).

f.w: thou hast made me to serve with thy sins

n: And yet—God Himself wipes out their sins for His own sake and chooses not to remember them. Forgiveness flows from His nature, not from Israel’s merit.
God invites Israel to court: remind Me of your case; argue it, if you think you are in the right.
Israel’s sin goes far back—to its “first father” (probably Jacob) and to its own spokesmen or leaders.

f.g: Likely Jacob, whose early life included deceit (Genesis 27).
Literally “interpreters” or spokesmen—priests and prophets meant to guide Israel.

n: So God disgraced the temple leaders and gave Israel over to destruction and scorn—a reference to the fall of Jerusalem and exile.
